slides.title: Prove the nightly match before finance switches over
slides.lead: Finance and engineering need a go/no-go decision grounded in replay results and exception ownership.

items.title: The decision
items.text: Authorize a sandbox validation of invoice matching between Billing and Ledger. Production posting remains a later decision.

items.title: The required proof
items.text: A complete batch must reconcile, duplicates must be harmless, and every held item must reach an accountable owner.

slides.title: The current handoff has no durable exception history
slides.lead: An analyst compares two exports each morning. A spreadsheet carries the corrections into the next run.

items.title: Export
items.text: Finance retrieves invoices from Billing and posted entries from Ledger.

items.title: Compare
items.text: The analyst matches order and account keys, then investigates unexplained differences.

items.title: Correct
items.text: Finance fixes a record and repeats the comparison without a shared replay log.

slides.title: A held record must explain what prevented posting
slides.lead: The new flow keeps clean matches moving while preserving the evidence needed to resolve an exception.

items.title: Read
items.text: Take a dated batch snapshot and retain its source identifiers.

items.title: Match
items.text: Compare account, order, currency and amount using approved rules.

items.title: Hold
items.text: Route ambiguity to an owner with the conflicting values visible.

items.title: Post
items.text: Write approved entries with a stable idempotency key.

slides.title: The first release ends at a reconciled nightly batch
slides.lead: The scope separates matching from changes to pricing or customer communications.

rows: Use a completed batch; do not add a real-time service.
Show the reason, owner and resolution history.
Repeat a batch without creating another journal entry.
Tell finance when the batch stalls or held items remain.

slides.title: Pricing and historical migration stay outside this scope
slides.lead: The engagement cannot absorb adjacent work through an implementation assumption.

items.title: Billing changes
items.text: Pricing rules, quote approvals and invoice generation stay in their existing systems. The service consumes their results.

items.title: Separate work
items.text: Historical invoice migration, customer statements and collections workflows need their own scope and acceptance decision.

slides.title: The adapter must preserve identity across retries
slides.lead: A durable run ledger connects the source snapshot, matching decision and posting receipt.

rows: Capture the completed batch and source keys.
Apply the approved rules to each candidate.
Post with a stable request identifier.
Check the prior receipt before retrying.

slides.title: Finance owns the exception decision
slides.lead: Engineering repairs technical failures. Business approval stays with the team responsible for the books.

rows: Correct the source mapping and replay the item.
Approve a correction with its reason recorded.
Resolve the receipt before retrying the request.

slides.title: A replay must not create a second journal entry
slides.lead: Run duplicate and timeout cases before a production posting path is considered.

rows: The second run creates no additional journal entry.
A post times out after acceptance
A receipt lookup resolves the outcome before retry.

slides.title: An ambiguous match must reach its owner
slides.lead: The resolution history must survive a correction and subsequent replay.

rows: A key maps to two accounts
The item is held without a guessed match.
The replay retains the original reason and correction.

slides.title: Advance only when each phase has usable evidence
slides.lead: The sequence leaves a reviewable result before the next implementation step begins.

items.title: Map
items.text: Finance signs the key mapping and exception categories.

items.title: Build
items.text: Engineering implements the reader, matcher and adapter in a sandbox.

items.title: Replay
items.text: The team tests a complete batch and the named failure cases.

items.title: Decide
items.text: The controller reviews the evidence and authorizes or defers cutover.

slides.title: A failed cutover must leave a workable morning process
slides.lead: The runbook preserves the current reconciliation process until the new service has passed acceptance.

items.title: Before switching
items.text: Capture the last completed batch, confirm the responsible engineer and record who can stop posting.

items.title: When a check fails
items.text: Pause the new posting path, reconcile accepted receipts, and return finance to the documented manual process.

slides.title: Approve validation after the missing inputs have owners
slides.lead: The team can begin when the mapping, test access and acceptance authority are recorded.

rows: Select a complete sample and its expected totals.
Approve keys, tolerances and exception ownership.
